title: Report Daily Session Counts by Tutor
prompt: A tutoring marketplace tracks session bookings in the `sessions` table and tutor profiles in the `tutors` table (modeled on education/training platform datasets). Each session record includes a `session_date` (stored as TEXT in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format), `tutor_id`, and a `status` code (stored as TEXT: '1' for completed, '2' for cancelled, '3' for no-show). The tutors table includes a `tutor_name` (with possible leading/trailing spaces) and a `subject_tags` TEXT array listing subjects the tutor teaches. You need to produce a daily report showing how many completed sessions (status = '1') each tutor had on each day in the week from '2024-03-04' through '2024-03-10' (inclusive). Every tutor must appear for every day in that range, even if they had zero completed sessions on that day. For each row, display `tutor_id`, `tutor_name` (trimmed and title-cased), `first_subject` (the first element of the subject_tags array), `session_date` (as a DATE type), `day_name` (the day of the week, e.g., 'Monday'), and `completed_count` (the count of completed sessions; use 0 when there are none, not NULL). Order the output by `session_date` ASC, then `tutor_id` ASC. Columns: tutor_id, tutor_name, first_subject, session_date, day_name, completed_count.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE tutors (tutor_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tutor_name TEXT, subject_tags TEXT[]); CREATE TABLE sessions (session_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tutor_id INT, session_date TEXT, status TEXT);
example_input_data: INSERT INTO tutors (tutor_id, tutor_name, subject_tags) VALUES (1, ' alice smith ', ARRAY['Math', 'Physics']), (2, 'bob jones  ', ARRAY['English']); INSERT INTO sessions (session_id, tutor_id, session_date, status) VALUES (101, 1, '2024-03-04', '1'), (102, 1, '2024-03-04', '1'), (103, 1, '2024-03-05', '2'), (104, 2, '2024-03-06', '1'), (105, 1, '2024-03-08', '1'), (106, 2, '2024-03-08', '3');

composite_moves: CROSS JOIN with tutors to fan-out
LEFT JOIN actuals with date cast

hints: You need every combination of tutor and date in the output, even when there are no sessions.
Use generate_series to create a date range from '2024-03-04' to '2024-03-10', then cross join it with the tutors table to form a skeleton.

Left join the skeleton to the sessions table (cast session_date to DATE first), filter for status = '1', aggregate with COUNT, and use COALESCE to turn NULLs into 0. Extract the day name with TO_CHAR and the first subject with subject_tags[1].
answer_key: WITH date_range AS (SELECT generate_series(DATE '2024-03-04', DATE '2024-03-10', INTERVAL '1 day')::date AS dt), skeleton AS (SELECT t.tutor_id, INITCAP(TRIM(t.tutor_name)) AS tutor_name, t.subject_tags[1] AS first_subject, d.dt AS session_date FROM tutors t CROSS JOIN date_range d) SELECT sk.tutor_id, sk.tutor_name, sk.first_subject, sk.session_date, TO_CHAR(sk.session_date, 'Day') AS day_name, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status = '1' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS completed_count FROM skeleton sk LEFT JOIN sessions s ON sk.tutor_id = s.tutor_id AND sk.session_date = s.session_date::date GROUP BY sk.tutor_id, sk.tutor_name, sk.first_subject, sk.session_date ORDER BY sk.session_date, sk.tutor_id;

_meta.scenario: a tutoring marketplace tracking session booking and tutor ratings
